correctness.rationale: Direct separation into first-only, second-only, and product-only edges gives three tensor operators. The first has free k and requires l to differ; the second has free j and requires i to differ; the third fixes i,l and requires both j,k to differ. Their sector eigenvalues are w(t-1), (u-1)v and (v-1)(w-1), respectively. Their sum is the stated eigenvalue; constants and sum-zero factors give the stated multiplicities even when a factor has size one. The uniform degree, two connected families of fixed-coordinate moves for a,b>=2, and the direct clique union when one factor is one establish the connectivity claims. Size and degree recover the product and sum of the factor sizes, and reversing the factor order and the two inputs gives the converse graph isomorphism. At (2,2) the five Cayley steps are the images of the coordinate steps of the five-cube modulo the antipodal vector, which gives Clebsch; the exact characteristic polynomial and common-neighbor identity agree. The matrix-tree product follows from regularity and simplicity of the degree eigenvalue for connected graphs. Independent exact characteristic polynomials from the raw adjacency rule matched for all nine pairs 1<=a,b<=3. The juxtaposition XZ and YZ in the frozen proof denotes entrywise intersection of equality indicators, not ordinary matrix multiplication; the separate-edge calculation avoids that notational ambiguity.
residual_risks: The graph convention must be exactly one equal entry. The independent finite checks do not substitute for the tensor proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither the degree nor the null law determines the exactly-one rectangular-band spectrum. In the common definition, the (2,2) graph is connected, so the proposed nontrivial independent block partition cannot be a stronger correct statement covering the claimed spectrum.

evidence: The prior lemma says adjacency requires agreement on the L-coordinate. For example, ((0,0),(0,0),(0,0)) and ((0,0),(1,1),(0,1)) are adjacent by first-only agreement, with product entries in different Green L-classes. First- and second-only moves together imply connectedness when a,b>=2.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The qualitative block assertion neither gives the sector numbers and multiplicities nor validly reduces the graph to independent Green-class components. Known regularity gives the single degree eigenvalue and supports factor recovery; these consequences are not the novelty basis.

originality.rationale: The exact-one graph definition and rectangular-band degree formula are prior; diagonalizing the complete-graph tensor factors is standard. Pass the explicit full spectrum and the structural conclusions specific to this graph family. The closest primary paper's similarly titled lemma gives no explicit sector spectrum, and its proposed disconnected block picture does not hold for the same adjacency.
residual_risks: An equivalent equality-relation fusion spectrum under other terminology cannot be excluded by bounded searches. No novelty is claimed for the underlying spectral machinery.

value.rationale: This is the full exact adjacency invariant of the natural regular rectangular-band family from the motivating paper, not an isolated computed size. It replaces degree-only information by a multiplicity formula valid for all factor sizes and clarifies the misleading disconnected-block picture. It also separates the connected and degenerate cases and puts the Clebsch instance and spanning-tree count into one family. Standard diagonalization alone does not identify the graph's sector eigenvalues.
residual_risks: Restricted to rectangular bands, with no claim of a new invariant for arbitrary semigroups or a new spectral technique.
